name: The Gatekeeper's Oath (fair copy)
description: A slim pamphlet, single-stitch bound, the paper cheap. Copies are made by junior archivists for any visitor who asks: the charter pays for the ink.
passage: Twelve lines, hand-copied in a young archivist's careful column. The margin has a single pencilled note in a different hand — *the one who wrote this oath was not a gatekeeper. Why is it still correct?* — and an ink-flick that was never wiped away.

name: A Note on the West Reading-Room
description: A single folded leaf left on the kettle-table. It bears no title and no date; the hand is Librarian Zhao's, but younger.
passage: The note is in Zhao's earlier hand, when his characters still had corners. It has been re-folded many times: the creases are soft with use.

name: The Sword Calamity — An Abridgment
description: A short chronicle, copied and re-copied, the abridgment of a longer work the Azure Cloud no longer holds. Priced against the labour of copying, not the weight of what it says.
passage: A half-hour's reading. The abridgment is careful with names and careless with dates — the archivists do not trust the dates. The last sentence is underlined so often the paper is worn thin beneath it.

name: Marginalia to the Sutra of Empty Sleeves
description: A bound photograph of the original — not a copy, a tracing — each marginal note reproduced with the exact slant, the exact weight, the exact bleed of the red ink. The committee of 1184 wrote these notes. Someone, much later, thought they ought to be readable without touching the original.
passage: You sit with the tracing a long time. The marginalia is in a hand that disagrees with itself from folio to folio — seven hands, perhaps, or one hand that had stopped agreeing with its owner. The seventh note, signed with the broken-strokes sign, feels addressed to you personally. It is not, of course. It was written eight hundred years before you were born. But that is exactly the sort of trick a library plays on a reader who has stayed too long.

name: Ninefold Azure Cuts — Commentary Copy
description: A sword-treatise bound in pale blue silk. The treatise itself is not the book's rare part; the rare part is the sixty pages of commentary added by nine successive inner-hall elders, each disagreeing with the last.
passage: The treatise is short and elegant: nine cuts, drawn in thick ink, no footwork noted. The commentary — sixty pages, nine elders — argues for sixty pages about the footwork. On the final page of commentary the ninth elder has written, in a larger hand: *the cuts are correct; the feet are different each time; this is the teaching.* Under her note, a tenth hand, recent, in red ink: *yes.*

name: The Decision Is This Peg — Committee Papers
description: A thick folio, the paper brittle, the stitching new: the archivists rebind it once a generation so the ink does not leave with the thread. Not on any public catalogue. It is not, properly, lent — only read, and only at the west table, and only when Librarian Zhao sets out the second cushion.
passage: You read the committee's papers through. They are not what the sect remembers. Six of the seven voted to keep the shelf. The seventh voted to seal. The vote was carried by the seventh alone, because the other six were persuaded — not of her argument, but of her willingness to go on arguing for as long as the sect remained. She won by patience. The six agreed to seal on the eleventh day because, they wrote, they had come to love her too much to outlive her. They drove the peg themselves. The seventh drove her own nail last, and locked the door from within. A marginal note in a much later hand names her: *Sister Willow of the Third Gate. She is buried not with the others but in the west wall of the library, behind the reading-room her body became.*

name: Torn Catalogue Page
description: A thick paper folio-page, torn crossways. The top half lists seven catalogue numbers in a neat archivist's hand. The bottom half is missing. The numbers, taken together, reference a single shelf — and that shelf has been locked for eight hundred years.

name: Sister Willow's Record
description: A small book of grey paper, the cover scorched but not burned through. Inside: a woman's hand, tight and patient, beginning *I write this knowing the peg will hold*. The Jadestep scholar who preserved it wrote, on the inside cover, in red ink: *If you find this, she has outlived us. Give her back to the Cloud.*

name: Black Banner Sash
description: A coarse black-lacquered sash, older than the gang it currently flies for. The Black Banner passes from brother to brother; each new bearer adds a red thread where the previous one fell. The sash is heavier on one side.

name: Stormwarden's Marginalia (smuggled copy)
description: A foundation-tier treatise: the private reading-notes of Stormwarden Gao on the Crane-sword sutras. Not sect-canonical. Gao is known to have said 'if the library wants a copy, the library can have a copy,' which the library took as license. Priced against the archivist who spent six months tracing it.
passage: Gao's notes are severe. The margins are wider than the text; he has written back at every line. In the hand of an old soldier: *the cut is the prayer, not the prayer before the cut.* And below, nine lines down: *the Crane is not the sword; the Crane is what the sword watches to remember it is not a hawk.* The manual does not teach a technique — Gao would not write one down that way — but after an afternoon of it you begin to see what he means about the flight of the blade.
